notes_list.title: Carbocations — Structure and Stability
notes_list.basic_overview: Carbocations are electron-deficient carbon centers commonly described as three-coordinate, approximately trigonal planar species with an empty p orbital.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Stability depends on hyperconjugation, inductive effects, resonance and solvation. Benzylic and allylic carbocations gain strong resonance stabilization.
notes_list.examples: tert-butyl, benzyl and allyl carbocations illustrate different stabilization modes.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Polar protic solvents can stabilize ions; strongly ionizing media favor ionization steps.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Identify empty p orbital. 2. Evaluate resonance. 3. Evaluate hyperconjugation/+I. 4. Check rearrangement pathways. 5. Consider solvent stabilization.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: For an SN1/E1 substrate, carbocation formation is commonly rate-determining under simple conditions. A more stable intermediate generally corresponds to a lower barrier, but the full transition-state environment matters.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not assume all tertiary carbocations are more stable than resonance-stabilized primary benzylic/allylic carbocations.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
